M1.reason: The outline in every side view (LEFT, RIGHT, TOP, BELOW) is a thin straight bar with a curved grey hook at one end. The brief asks for a pump-action shotgun with a receiver, barrel, pump, trigger and a folding stock whose end hooks over. None of those forms are in the silhouette. The hook is the only part that resembles the brief, and it reads as a crowbar's head, not a stock.

M2.reason: Length measures 31.6 against the brief's 30, a 5.2% difference, within the 15% band. The brief gives no width or height, so only length is held. The 1.9 by 7.1 cross-section is not held to any number the brief gives.

M3.reason: The brief's parts, listed down to the small ones: barrel, receiver, a pump (forend) and its grip, trigger and trigger guard, sights or bead, magazine tube, a folding stock, and the stock's hooked end. The asset has a red handle and a grey curved head, and nothing else. There is no pump, no trigger or guard, no stock, no sights and no magazine tube, in any of the ten views, the first-person view or the attack frames. Missing parts cap M3 at 0.

M4.reason: The brief asks for black metal with a wooden or dark pump. The asset's main body is saturated red (ten side views and the lineup), and only the hook is grey. The black metal region and the pump's dark wood are both absent, so the colour of the main region is wrong.

M5.reason: The brief names no markings, but it does name a pump and a receiver, which would carry panel lines, a sight rib and wood grain. The asset shows only flat shading on a plain bar and a faint sheen on the hook. The red paint is what the brief does not want.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the rubric caps M6 for this kind. The line-up (lineup.png, A to D) was passed by the line-up test: the judges picked the asset as the odd one out only at about chance. That result says it looks like a Valve prop among Valve props; it does not say it is a shotgun, which M1 and M3 already cover.

M7.reason: The brief gives no front, but a shotgun's front is its muzzle and receiver, and neither is in the asset. The front view is a tiny red end with a grey point, which is not identifiable as a muzzle. The bar stands on its own origin in the side views, but nothing in the asset shows which way is its front.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. The asset has 76 triangles, under the median of 138 for Half-Life's props of its kind, under the three-quarter mark of 187 and under twice the median. The side and angle views show a solid bar and hook with no openings, inside-out faces or floating parts.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset is a large red bar filling the upper left of the frame. No hand is seen on it, and it does not sit where the game's shotgun sits at the lower right, which is the same frame with an orange glove on it. In attack.png no hand is drawn on the bar, and the bar only moves across the frame. The asset is not seen to be held, so it cannot be seen to leave the hands.
